_comment: Single source of truth for macro indicators (Plan A Tier 1). NOT YET wired into index.html render — see PLAN-macro-json.md for remaining steps. Each value carries a 'source' = the FRED / Trading Economics series ID it will auto-fetch from in Tier 2.

us10y.label: US 10Y Treasury
us10y.note: still pinned near ~5.2% into mid-October (5.24% on 1 Oct) — around the highest level since the 2007–08 financial crisis; the 10Y has climbed ~100+bps YTD (opened 2026 at 4.16%). Fed funds 3.75–4.00% after the 16 Sept hike; next FOMC 27–28 Oct, one more hike projected this year. Levels for 16–20 Oct not independently verified — see live macro board.

fedFunds.label: Fed Funds Rate
fedFunds.note: first hike in 3 years, unanimous FOMC decision; the Fed's own Summary of Economic Projections points to at least one more hike before year-end

usCPI.label: US CPI (YoY)
usCPI.note: August print (BLS, released 11 Sept): headline CPI +3.4% YoY, unchanged from July; core eased to its lowest annual pace since March 2021.

usPCE.label: US PCE (YoY)
usPCE.note: not independently re-verified this cycle; watch alongside the next CPI print

dxy.label: Dollar Index (DXY)
dxy.note: at a two-month high alongside the 10Y spike; held above ~100 as of 25 Sept. Exact intraday level not independently re-verified this cycle.

source.caveat: DXY proper is ICE; DTWEXBGS is FRED's broad trade-weighted USD index — close proxy, label accordingly

biRate.label: Bank Indonesia Rate
biRate.note: Bank Indonesia held the BI-Rate at 5.75% at the 22–23 September 2026 meeting — a stability decision as the rupiah was under pressure from rising US yields and a firm dollar

usdidr.label: USD/IDR
usdidr.note: around ~17,900–17,940 into mid-October (~17,936 on 15 Oct) — pressing the 18,000 line as US yields and the dollar stay firm; Bank Indonesia held at 5.75% on 22–23 Sept. Levels for 16–20 Oct not independently verified — see live macro board

gold.label: Gold (XAU)
gold.note: holding a ~$4,130–4,200 band through mid-October — low ~$4,125 (LBMA fix $4,124.55 on 8 Oct), back near ~$4,180 by 13 Oct — rising 10Y yields and a firm dollar keep capping the safe-haven bid; still well below January's ~$5,300–5,600 record

source.caveat: no free FRED/TE daily series; keep manual or use a market-data API in a later tier

wti.label: WTI Crude
wti.note: reversed back up from the early-Oct ~$82 dip to ~$96 — November futures settled ~$97.97 on 15 Oct (+~6% on the week). Ships are transiting Hormuz again (40+ in 24h) but flows run ~two-thirds of baseline and the risk premium returns without a formal US–Iran deal. Nothing formally signed, risk stays two-sided; see live macro board.
